Technology stocks were dropping in late trade, giving in to the post-FOMC slump and dragging the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 to a nearly 1.9% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index declined almost 4.1% this afternoon.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Facebook ( FB ) Wednesday retreated Wednesday despite denying it allowed outside firms to access users' personal data without their permission, disputing a New York Times report it provided other tech firms and advertisers with nearly unlimited access to the social network's vast stores of members' interests, preferences and contacts. "We've taken a number of steps this year to limit developers' access to people's Facebook information," Facebook's director of developer platforms and programs, Konstantinos Papamiltiadis, said in a blog post.
In other sector news:
(+) Jabil Circuit ( JBL ) pushed out to a more than 14% advance on Wednesday after the electronic components manufacturer reported a 12.5% increase in fiscal Q1 net income to $0.90 per share, beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.02 per share.
(+) Autodesk ( ADSK ) climbed over 3% in recent Wednesday trading after Stifel Nicolaus began analyst coverage with a buy rating and a $163 price target.
(-) Micron Technology ( MU ) slid more than 8% to its lowest share price in more than a year at $31.28 each after projecting non-GAAP fiscal Q2 net income in a range of $1.65 to $1.85 per share, trailing analyst estimates by at least $0.60 per share.
